tldr: DeepSeek's flagship V4 Pro entered late July already under scrutiny, benchmarked head-to-head against Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on cost, license, and serving price. Within days a rival low-cost model was already beating it on price-performance.
whats_new: DeepSeek's own retrained V4-Flash — the cheaper, faster sibling model — now beats flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks.
why_it_matters: Teams running DeepSeek for agent workloads should re-benchmark before assuming Pro is still the right default: the higher-priced flagship no longer leads on agent tasks against its own cheaper sibling.

status.detail: DeepSeek's cheaper V4-Flash variant has overtaken flagship V4 Pro on agent benchmarks, following earlier comparisons that were already unfavorable to Pro on price-performance.

beats.headline: V4 Pro benchmarked against Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on cost, license, and performance
beats.summary: A three-way trillion-scale MoE comparison put V4 Pro alongside two open-weight rivals on benchmarks, licensing terms, and serving cost.

beats.headline: Rival Laguna S 2.1 undercuts V4 Pro on price and performance
beats.summary: A newly released low-cost model was pitched as cheaper than DeepSeek's own V4-Flash and better than V4 Pro.

beats.headline: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash beats V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks
beats.summary: DeepSeek's cheaper sibling model now outperforms the flagship Pro on agent-focused evaluations.

open_questions: Does DeepSeek reposition V4-Flash as the default choice for agent workloads, or keep Pro as the flagship despite the benchmark loss?
Do independent evals confirm V4-Flash's nine-benchmark lead over Pro, or is this DeepSeek's own reported result?
Does V4-Flash's pricing undercut V4 Pro enough to change the serving-cost calculus for teams already running Pro?
take_for_builders: Running DeepSeek V4 Pro for agent workloads? Re-benchmark against V4-Flash before your next deployment — DeepSeek's own numbers now put the cheaper sibling ahead on agent tasks.
